To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the outdoor regional living collections of mainland Portugal are expected to be outside their original bioclimatc neighbourhood by 2081, under the Intergovernmenta Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) A2 scenario, while under the B2 scenario most of them are expected to be inside that neighbourhood.

the outdoor regional living collections of mainland Portugal are expected to be inside the predefined bioc limatic neighbourhood by 2020, according to the B1 scenario, and by 2050, according to all considered scenarios.
, according to downscaled climate change scenario A2, all sites will be outside their bioclimatic niche, while according to B2 scenario all will be inside, although sometimes marginaly so.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of global climate change scenarios on the regional living plant collections in mainland Portugal.
the identification and analysis of the impacts of climate changes, in the short, medium and long term, on the outdoor living plant collections in mainland Portugal.
the impact of climate change on outdoor plant collections, with a focus on the Portuguese mainland.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the outdoor regional living plants collections are not threatened by climate change, but rather by the way we are managing it.
the outdoor regional living collections of mainland Portugal are expected to be severely impacted by climate change.
the B2 scenario should be the one to follow, as the most sustainable, in the light of the outdoor regional plant collections’ conservation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the outdoor plant collections of Portugal will be affected by the expected changes in climate, with the potential for a loss in species composition, but that the implementation of the B2 scenario could delay the impacts of climate changes.
the outdoor regional living collections are a good starting point for the development of a more detailed regional approach, as they are a good indicator of what is going on in the region.

the implementation of the A2 scenario will result in a loss of the bioclimatically suitable areas for outdoor plant conservation, while the B2 scenario will result, at least for a while, in a maintenance of those areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the outdoor living plant collections are not only a tool for conservation but also a tool for the understanding of the impact of climate change.

it is possible to predict the future biogeographical shift of outdoor living plant collections and that the B2 scenario is a very important tool in this process, allowing us to better understand the future of these collections.

, while the outdoor regional living collections can play a key role in the adaptation process, their conservation and management should be planned in the light of the predicted changes in their bioclimatic conditions, in order to avoid a significant loss of their species diversity.
